name: building-907
estimated: some sizes, with a photograph as a reference: the places and heights of the band of glazing on the hall's west-north-west end and of the pale strip across it, and of the annex's windows and doors; and the faces no photograph shows, drawn plainly
refs_note: the folder of refs/ that holds the reference views (views.json, masks/), which refine, compare, metrics, sky_mask and the viewer's ?sv= read: refs/photos (gitignored), whose views tools/photo_camera.py writes. Its one photograph is taken from the street west-south-west of the building, about 27 m from the annex's corner nearest it, through a lens of about 72 degrees across, looking up 6.3 degrees; its camera is fitted to the annex's two corners on its south-south-west face (their tops and feet) and the vault's crown on the hall's west-north-west end, with the annex's two corners and the left edge of a pillar before the gates as verticals, held 1.6 m over the LiDAR's ground (1.93 m fitted; rms 2.45 px)

building.title: Building 907 (907), University of Auckland
building.note: outline: building 907's outer ring from the main project's campus.json, in the map's frame; it chooses the crop box and the building's own points (frame.near_outline, measure and topview). The site replaces block 907 by its id.

origin.note: the campus origin, as in campus.json; the landmark's local metres = NZTM (EPSG:2193) minus the NZTM of this point, with grid north

door.note: before the glazed door under a small canopy on the annex's west-north-west face, as the photograph shows it (the campus map records no lobby or entrance in 907, and OpenStreetMap no entrance within 120 m): on the yard 1.5 m out from that face (u 23.3, w 17.8 in the building's frame; (-23.3, 17.8) in the view frame). The LiDAR's ground within 1 m: 22 returns, p10/p50/p90 53.514/53.556/53.597 m

frame.method: LiDAR building points (class 6) more than min_above m above the ground and within near_outline m of building.outline
frame.thresholds_note: min_above and tower_above 9 m over the provisional ground: the frame is the top of the hall's barrel vault, whose crown stands about 10 m over the ground and its eaves about 6.5 m, and the annex (7.5 to 8 m) is left out; the centre is that top's, the axis its principal axis (axis_from left out), bearing 284.90 deg, along the vault: within 0.24 deg of its crown line fitted to the LiDAR (285.13 deg), and the eaves keep their distance from it to 0.1 m along the hall. The walls axis is not used: on this roof it gave 287.7 deg, along which the eaves drift 1 m over 30 m. x runs along the vault toward its east-south-east end, z faces south-south-west, toward the annex; all three lowered by 0.37 m with the ground set at the door (step 7), so that they pick the same points

ground_note: the LiDAR's ground at the door (step 7, 2026-11-09); the provisional ground was 53.19 m, the median LiDAR ground in the first crop box, from which the heights in parts/common.js are measured (its H moves them on to this ground)
crop_note: 45 m round the outline, so that the crop box takes in the street west-south-west of the annex where the photograph is taken (25 m left its camera outside, with no LiDAR ground under it to hold its height)

light.note: estimated: the photograph was taken on an overcast, wet day, every face it shows without sun. The viewer's sun at 65 deg round (behind the building, seen from the camera) and 40 up leaves those faces to the sky's light; the building's luma p50 232 with the sun at 240 deg and 60 up at exposure 0.7, then with the sun behind 202 at 1.2, 176 at 0.9 and 149 at 0.65, against the photograph's 150 (counted in the model's screen box)
